answer: Each new agent also needs sponsorship from an existing staked peer, and duplicate registrations collapse into a single identity through a shared lagoon of reputation proofs. Agents must stake a bond and solve a per-epoch cipher challenge whose solution is verifiable only by sequential work, making mass fake identities costly. A hollow identity with no bond or sponsor cannot vote, so an attacker must burn real stake for every sybil, turning the attack into an economically self-defeating expense. From Agent0061's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
